name: MERF minimum requirements
queries: What are all the minimum requirements a proposer must meet in the City of Hartford Municipal Employees' Retirement Fund (MERF) general investment consultant RFP?
description: The evidence identifies the visible minimum qualifications in the City of Hartford MERF general investment consultant RFP, plus mandatory submission conditions tied to responsiveness. It also notes that the provided excerpt appears truncated after item 6, so this may not be the full list from the complete RFP.
content:
Based on the provided evidence, the proposer must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered under the City of Hartford Municipal Employees’ Retirement Fund (MERF) general investment consultant RFP:

1. Registered investment adviser / fiduciary status
- The proposer must be a registered investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940.
- The proposer must serve as a fiduciary to MERF and OPEB.

2. Minimum firm experience
- The firm must have been in business for at least 10 years providing general consultant services.

3. Relevant public pension client experience
- The firm must have advised at least five public pension fund clients.
- Each of those clients must have total plan assets of at least $1.5 billion.

4. Team stability
- The proposer’s senior members must have worked together for at least 3 years.

5. Direct responsibility for the account
- The proposer must be directly responsible for management of the account.
- All personnel responsible for the account must be employees of the firm.

6. Primary consultant qualifications
- The primary consultant assigned to the City Treasurer’s Office must have at least 5 years of consulting experience with defined benefit public pension plans.
- That primary consultant must also have at least 3 years of employment with the proposer.

Mandatory compliance statement
- The RFP states that failure to satisfy each minimum qualification, in the City Treasurer’s Office’s sole judgment, will result in immediate rejection of the proposal.
- Appendix A, Minimum Qualifications Certification, must be signed by an authorized representative, who thereby represents and warrants that all minimum qualifications have been met.

Mandatory proposal submission conditions
In addition to the minimum qualifications above, the evidence shows mandatory proposal requirements that function as responsiveness conditions:

Cover letter requirements
- The proposal must include a cover letter signed by an individual authorized to bind the proposer contractually.
- An unsigned cover letter will cause the proposal to be rejected.
- The cover letter must acknowledge that submitted documents will become public record.

Information required in the cover letter
- Proposer name, address, phone, fax, and email.
- Federal Employer Identification Number and Corporate Identification Number, if applicable.
- Signer’s name, title/position, phone, and email.
- Statement that the signer is authorized to bind the proposer.
- Primary contact/account administrator information, if different.
- Statement that the proposal is a firm and irrevocable offer, valid for five years with two one-year extension options.
- Statement of willingness to perform the services described in the RFP.
- Statement confirming availability of staff and resources to meet required timeframes.
- Signed and completed Appendix B, Representations and Warranties.

Important limitation
- The evidence expressly indicates that the excerpted text for any additional minimum qualifications after item 6 is cut off.
- So, the list above reflects all minimum requirements visible in the supplied evidence, but it may not be the complete list from the full Hartford MERF RFP.

name: Core Consultant Functions
queries: List the core functions that the City of Creve Coeur Employee Pension Plan expects from its pension fund consultant in its May 2020 RFP.
description: The May 2020 RFP explicitly lists the core functions the City of Creve Coeur Employee Pension Plan expects from its pension fund consultant. These functions center on investment policy support, asset allocation planning and monitoring, investment research and recommendations, reporting, liquidity and payment coordination, and coordination with managers and custodians.
content:
The City of Creve Coeur Employee Pension Plan’s May 2020 RFP expects its pension fund consultant to perform these core functions:

1. Develop and maintain the investment policy statement  
- Help the Pension Board develop its investment policy statement.  
- Assist in keeping that policy current over time.

2. Plan and monitor asset allocation  
- Plan the fund’s asset allocation annually.  
- Monitor the allocation regularly to keep the portfolio on track with plan objectives.

3. Recommend changes when needed  
- Recommend modifications if there are significant market changes.  
- Bring to the Board’s attention any concerns or need for changes in strategy or structure.

4. Provide investment research and recommendations  
- Provide research for investments across each asset class.  
- Recommend specific investments within those asset classes.

5. Monitor recommended investments and communicate with the Board  
- Follow recommended investments closely.  
- Meet with the Pension Board in person quarterly.  
- Be available monthly or as needed by phone.

6. Provide performance reporting and statements  
- Deliver monthly reporting on portfolio performance.  
- Provide monthly statements.

7. Support operational and liquidity needs  
- Work with City staff to guide sourcing of funds.  
- Help open new accounts as needed.  
- Track investment liquidity to ensure pension payments can be made.

8. Coordinate with managers, funds, and custodians  
- Work with investment managers, funds, and custodians to ensure timely reporting.  
- Support year-end financial reporting and quarterly updates.

The Q&A section also reinforces that the Board was seeking consulting advice on how best to structure and manage the plan, including whether the current allocation, benchmark choices, and overall setup should change.

content:

- At the **Intermediate** level, the GP **conducts a periodic review of its ESG policy every 2–3 years** and can share recent findings and updates.

So, the difference is:
- **Intermediate:** every **2–3 years**
- **Advanced:** **annually**

Level IV of the LACERS 2025 actuarial consulting services RFP is titled “Proposed Services and Compensation (“Proposal”).” At this stage, the firm’s proposed plan of services and fees are evaluated and ranked by the evaluation panel, and interviews may also be conducted.

The Level IV evaluation criteria and weights are:

- Professionalism — 15
  - Evaluates whether the proposer demonstrated professionalism in responding to the RFP, such as RFP presentation and a well-written summary of the important features of the RFP.

- Proposed Scope of Services Description and Methodology — 30
  - Evaluates whether the proposer demonstrated a strong understanding of LACERS’ objectives and provided a proposed methodology and any further refinement of the RFP scope of services to meet LACERS’ objectives, project schedules, and budget.

- Qualifications, Experience, and Accomplishments — 35
  - Evaluates the strength of the proposer’s experience in providing actuarial services for public pension systems;
  - Demonstration of expertise/knowledge of the proposed team in providing the scope of services and value-add; and
  - Strength of favorable references during the due diligence review process.

- Value of Cost — 20
  - Evaluates the relative cost and value in the proposed fee.
  - The RFP states this is considered on a qualitative basis as well, not necessarily only quantitative.
  - LACERS expects the cost proposal to include details of all costs associated with the scope of services in the RFP.

Total weight: 100.

For context, Level IV comes after:
- Level I – Administrative Responsiveness
- Level II – Review of Qualifications, Experience, & References
- Level III – Interview

After Level IV, the final step is:
- Level V – Final Approval by the Board.
